bug_report_content: Joda - Time / Bugs / #141 Bug on withLaterOffsetAtOverlap method Join/Login Business Software Open Source Software For Vendors Blog About More Articles Create SourceForge Podcast Site Documentation Subscribe to our Newsletter Support Request Bug on withLaterOffsetAtOverlap method Project moved to GitHub Brought to you by: broneill , scolebourne This project can now be found here. Summary Files Reviews Support Code Svn Tickets ▾ Bugs Feature Requests News Discussion Donate Menu ▾ ▴ Create Ticket View Stats Group v1.0_(example) Searches Changes Closed Tickets Open Tickets Help Formatting Help #141 Bug on withLaterOffsetAtOverlap method Status: closed Owner: Stephen Colebourne Labels: Joda-Time (76) Priority: 5 Updated: 2012-10-08 Created: 2012-01-20 Creator: Hood Wilson Gusso Silva Private: No The method withLaterOffsetAtOverlap created to workaround the issue 3192457 seems to not be working at all. I won´t write many info about the problem to solve because the issue 3192457 have this info indeed. But If something is unclear I can answer on the comments. Problem demonstration: TimeZone.setDefault(TimeZone.getTimeZone("America/Sao_Paulo")); DateTimeZone.setDefault( DateTimeZone.forID("America/Sao_Paulo") ); DateTime dtch ; { dtch = new DateTime(2012,2,25,5,5,5,5).millisOfDay().withMaximumValue() ; System.out.println( dtch ) ; // prints : 2012-02-25 T23 : 59 : 59.999 -02 : 00 // Were are at the first 23 :** of the day . // At this point dtch have the -03 : 00 offset } { dtch = dtch.plus(60001) ; System.out.println( dtch ) ; // prints : 2012-02-25 T23 : 01 : 00.000 -03 : 00 // Were are at the first minute of the second 23 :** of the day . Ok its correct // At this point dtch have the -03 : 00 offset } { dtch = dtch.withEarlierOffsetAtOverlap() ; System.out.println( dtch ) ; // prints : 2012-02-25 T23 : 01 : 00.000 -02 : 00 // Were are at the first minute of the first 23 :** of the day . Ok its correct // At this point dtch have the -02 : 00 offset ( because we called withEarlierOffsetAtOverlap () ) // This method is working perfectly } { dtch = dtch.withLaterOffsetAtOverlap() ; System.out.println( dtch ) ; // prints : 2012-02-25 T23 : 01 : 00.000 -02 : 00 // Were are at the first minute of the first 23 :** of the day . // Here is the problem we should have a -03 : 00 offset here since we called withLaterOffsetAtOverlap () expecting to change to the second 23 :** of the day } On the last two brackets we can see that withLaterOffsetAtOverlap is not undoing withEarlierOffsetAtOverlap as it should ( and not even working at all ) Discussion Hood Wilson Gusso Silva - 2012-01-20 On the first bracket I did a mistake on the comment as we can see in the print //At this point dtch have the -03:00 offset should be //At this point dtch have the -02:00 offset If you would like to refer to this comment somewhere else in this project, copy and paste the following link: Stephen Colebourne - 2012-02-02 A bad test and an incomplete test failed to show the problem you saw. The code is now rewritten to handle the problem in a different way, which should work (raise another bug if not) If you would like to refer to this comment somewhere else in this project, copy and paste the following link: Log in to post a comment. ✕
